name: Design Space Exploration using Software Simulators
description: This course introduces students to Design Space Exploration (DSE) as a systematic methodology for evaluating architectural design choices in modern processors and systems-on-chip. It begins by motivating the need for DSE and explaining fundamental performance, power, and area (PPA) trade-offs. Students are then introduced to simulation-based evaluation, contrasting functional and cycle-accurate simulators, with hands-on exposure to tools such as QEMU and gem5. The role of benchmarks and workloads is emphasized through representative suites like SPEC, PARSEC, and MiBench, including practical execution of MiBench on both QEMU and gem5. The course explores key architectural components through focused DSE studies on cache hierarchies, multicore systems, on-chip interconnects, and memory subsystems, allowing students to vary parameters and analyze metrics such as IPC and miss rate. The course followed by physical-aware DSE, where power, area, and frequency constraints are incorporated using tools such as McPAT, CACTI, and OpenROAD. The course concludes with an introduction to RTL simulation and demonstrates how pre-RTL architectural exploration connects to RTL and physical design flows.
prerequisites:
Basic knowledge in computer architecture, including cache, memory, and processor concepts.
Basic knowledge in Programming(C/C++/Python)
